facts.value: The rule that no book may be lent was held so firmly that King Charles I was refused a loan in 1645.
facts.quote: even King Charles I was refused permission to borrow a book in 1645
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://visit.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/plan-your-visit/history-bodleian' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'even King Charles I was refused permission to borrow a book in 1645'

facts.value: The library had no heating until 1845 and no artificial lighting until 1929.
facts.quote: with no heating until 1845 and no artificial lighting until 1929, the number of users should not be overestimated
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://visit.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/plan-your-visit/history-bodleian' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'no heating until 1845 and no artificial lighting until 1929'

facts.value: In 1550 the Dean of Christ Church stripped the university library of all its books to purge Catholic traces, and some were burnt.
facts.quote: the Dean of Christ Church, hoping to purge the English church of all traces of Catholicism including ‘superstitious books and images’, removed all the library’s books – some to be burnt
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://visit.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/plan-your-visit/history-bodleian' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'removed all the library'

facts.value: The Bodleian also held pictures, sculptures, coins and medals, and curiosities including a stuffed crocodile from Jamaica.
facts.quote: The Bodleian also housed pictures, sculptures, coins and medals, and ‘curiosities’ (including a stuffed crocodile from Jamaica)
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://visit.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/plan-your-visit/history-bodleian' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'stuffed crocodile from Jamaica'

facts.value: An underground book store dug beneath Radcliffe Square in 1909-12 was the largest of its kind in the world at the time.
facts.quote: an underground book store was excavated beneath Radcliffe Square in 1909–12; it was the largest such store in the world at the time
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://visit.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/plan-your-visit/history-bodleian' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'underground book store was excavated beneath Radcliffe Square'

facts.value: In 2025 the library unveiled a 13th-century Old French New Testament. Ultraviolet light showed erased inscriptions of three members of the English royal family who owned it in the 1400s.
facts.quote: ultraviolet light has revealed a series of erased inscriptions showing the manuscript was subsequently owned by three members of the English royal family in the 1400s
